summary: strtod-style converter: skips leading whitespace using a character-type table (or an encoding-aware fallback), parses the numeric string via EncodingLocaleDetectionFromParseResult, and returns the parsed double, handling infinity/NaN/range flag bits and setting TLS errno 34 (ERANGE) on non-finite results.

local_names.v4: parse-result descriptor (flags dword, end pointer, value)

operations.description: Skip leading whitespace: while the current byte classifies as space (bit 8 of the off_5E69C8 character-type table when cbMultiByte <= 1, else CharacterEncodingConvertViaLookupTableFallback(char, 8)), advance i.
Strlen(i) measures the remaining string; its result is unused by the caller flow.
EncodingLocaleDetectionFromParseResult(v9, i) parses the numeric token and returns a descriptor double* v4 carrying a flag dword at [0] and an end pointer at [1].
If a2 is non-null, write the end pointer past the parsed number into *a2.
Parse-flag test: if (v5 & 0x240) != 0 (range/format failure) take the error return; otherwise continue with finite/infinity/NaN handling.
Sign check: current character *i == 45 (ASCII '-') negates the infinity value; this is the packet guard this:0x0 == 45.
Infinity branch: when flags & 0x81, the value is +dbl_5E9990 (or -dbl_5E9990 when preceded by '-').
NaN branch: when flags & 0x100 the value is 0.0; when no special flag is set, return v4[2] as the plain parsed value without touching errno.
The non-finite path stores errno 34 (ERANGE) into the TLS slot via TLSOffsetGetter and returns the infinity or NaN value.
Error return: when flag 0x240 is set, return 0.0 and, if a2, set *a2 = a1 (the unconsumed start of the string).

unresolved: Flag-bit meanings (0x81 infinity, 0x100 NaN, 0x240 range/format) are inferred from the branch structure, not labelled in packet evidence.
Character class bit 8 is interpreted as whitespace per strtod convention.
